title: Life Sprint
premise: A fast-paced single-screen life simulator where each choice advances a year, forcing the player to balance work, learning, recovery, and social life while trying to survive and climb the career ladder.
interaction_model: Turn-based tap/click choice game with four recurring actions on a single mobile-friendly screen; each input immediately updates stats, age, events, and presentation feedback.
objective: Survive the long-term grind, avoid health collapse, grow money and skills, earn promotions, and ideally complete a full century-long life run.
progression: Linear stat-based progression driven by yearly action choices, skill thresholds for higher-paying careers, probabilistic promotions, and random life events that create setbacks or boosts.
theme: Compressed modern adult life as a neon arcade run, combining career pressure, self-care, personal growth, and burnout management.
mood: Bright, playful, and arcadey on the surface, but tinged with stress, hustle, and burnout risk underneath.
likely_audience: players who enjoy stat-balancing life games
players who like short replayable runs
confidence_notes: High confidence in the main loop because all core mechanics are explicit in the single-file JavaScript.
High confidence that the intended fantasy is life/career balancing rather than pure idle play because every turn requires a deliberate action.
Moderate confidence in the exact genre label; it overlaps life simulator, resource management, and light survival framing.
Low uncertainty about presentation tone because the UI, copy, and audio all reinforce a neon arcade life-run identity.
recreation_prompt: Create a mobile-first single-screen arcade life simulator called 'Life Sprint' where the player starts at age 18 and every tap advances one full year of life. Present four main actions at all times: work to earn money but lose morale and health, study/train to gain skills but spend money, relax/recover to regain morale and a little health, and socialize/network to raise morale at a cash cost. Track visible stats for age, money, health, morale, skills, and current career tier. Use skill thresholds to unlock a ladder of better jobs with higher salaries, but make promotions somewhat random so the player must keep pushing. Add passive yearly wear each turn so health and morale naturally decline over time, then layer in occasional random life events that can add bonuses, bills, burnout hits, audits, pet boosts, or other short text outcomes. End the run if health reaches zero from exhaustion, and also allow a successful ending if the player survives to age 100. Frame the whole experience with a polished neon sci-fi arcade presentation: glassy HUD panels, an animated age-based avatar, floating feedback text for gains and losses, short event logs, celebratory and danger reaction overlays, and energetic UI sound effects with looping background music. Keep controls simple, readable, and touch-friendly, with the feeling of a fast replayable life-management run rather than a deep spreadsheet sim.
